item.content:encoded:
THE Police Sharks will look to continue their winning streak in the Vodafone Cup after defeating City Storms 18-8 in round 6 of the competition at the Buckhurst Park last Saturday.

The Sharks combined solid defence with clinical finish to keep City Storms at bay throughout the contest and claim valuable points in the competition. Vice-captain of the side Arthur Nawaqanigauna said the victory reflected the hard work the team had put in despite the demands of serving as police officers.

“Apart from our work as police officers, we make time to train and prepare for our games. It hasn’t been easy, but the boys have shown great commitment.”

He said discipline and teamwork had been key to the side’s success, both on and off the field.

“Our work requires discipline every day, and we bring that same attitude onto the rugby field. Everyone plays for each other, and that’s what helped us get the win.”

The vice-captain praised City Storms for providing a tough contest and said the Sharks would continue working on areas that needed improvement as the competition progresses.

He also thanked the team’s supporters and fellow police officers for their encouragement, saying the side would remain focused on maintaining its momentum in the Vodafone Cup.

item.title: Nadi runs over Kadavu under-20 in opener
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi Under-20 delivered a ruthless attacking display to overpower Kadavu Rugby Under-20, 55-10 at King Charles Park in Nadi yesterday. The Nadi side wasted little time asserting their authority, crossing for the opening try in the 11th minute to take a 7-0 lead.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi Under-20 delivered a ruthless attacking display to overpower Kadavu Rugby Under-20, 55-10 at King Charles Park in Nadi yesterday.

The Nadi side wasted little time asserting their authority, crossing for the opening try in the 11th minute to take a 7-0 lead.

The hosts doubled their advantage four minutes later when tighthead prop Semesa Tuivunilagi powered over for a well-worked try.

First five-eighth Senivalati Senileba added the conversion to extend the lead to 14-0.

The match took a dramatic turn in the 25th minute when Nadi lock Lasarusa Luma received a red card for a dangerous tackle, while Kadavu halfback Inia Mulevoro was shown a yellow card in the same incident.

Despite being reduced to 14 men, Nadi continued to dominate proceedings. Second five-eighth Iveri Momo crossed for another try shortly afterwards, with Senileba converting to make it 21-0.

Blindside wing Kavekini Tubuilea then added another five-pointer in the 36th minute, although the conversion attempt drifted wide.

Nadi continued to pile on the pressure and headed into halftime with a commanding 31-0 advantage.

The second half began in perfect fashion for the home side as hooker Sikeli Cawe crossed just 40 seconds after the restart to keep the scoreboard ticking over.

Openside flanker Kamenieli Rasaku added another converted try in the 50th minute, stretching the margin to 43-0.

Nadi’s relentless attack continued in the 64th minute when centre Erami Bokoi dotted down before fullback Iliesa Nukuse converted to make it 50-0.

Kadavu finally got on the scoreboard in the 70th minute through a penalty goal from first five-eighth Saula Koroiboila, reducing the deficit to 50-3.

Nadi lock Pita Ratuloco crossed in the 76th minute for the hosts’ final try to take the score to 55-3.

Kadavu showed determination until the final whistle, scoring a converted try in the dying moments to add another seven points to the scoreboard.

However, it was Nadi who produced an outstanding all-round performance to secure a convincing 55-10 victory in front of their home supporters.

item.title: Malolo U20 overcomes Taveuni in rugby thriller
item.description: MALOLO U20 side produced a determined performance to overcome Taveuni U20 32-24 in a thrilling encounter at Lawaqa Park yesterday. The match was a closely fought battle as both teams displayed intensity and commitment, but it was Malolo who held their composure in the crucial moments to secure the victory.
item.content:encoded:
MALOLO U20 side produced a determined performance to overcome Taveuni U20 32-24 in a thrilling encounter at Lawaqa Park yesterday.

The match was a closely fought battle as both teams displayed intensity and commitment, but it was Malolo who held their composure in the crucial moments to secure the victory.

Malolo captain Sikeli Ukauka dedicated the win to their supporters, coaches, and management, acknowledging the challenges the team had faced in their preparation.

“Thank God for his guidance and protection on us. I thank the coaches and management; we were able to win this game because of their support,” Ukauka said.

“Few months back we were facing challenges, but we thank God for his love and the players for working together as a team.”

Ukauka said the victory was a reflection of the team’s unity and the hard work put in by the players despite the difficulties they encountered leading into the competition.

The win marks an important milestone for Malolo U20 as they continue their campaign, with the side looking to build on the confidence gained from the hard-fought victory.

item.title: Vusama’s fight for the dream
item.description: KINISALOTE Vusama has had to overcome more than challenges on the rugby league field to reach the opportunity now waiting for her in Australia. The 20-year-old from Naboutini, Serua, with maternal links to Baravi in Navakasiga, Bua, is one of five Fiji Bulikula players selected for the Rise Rookie Tour – Harvey Norman Invitational.
item.content:encoded:
KINISALOTE Vusama has had to overcome more than challenges on the rugby league field to reach the opportunity now waiting for her in Australia.

The 20-year-old from Naboutini, Serua, with maternal links to Baravi in Navakasiga, Bua, is one of five Fiji Bulikula players selected for the Rise Rookie Tour – Harvey Norman Invitational.

For Vusama, the tour represents another step towards the biggest goal of her rugby league career — securing an NRLW contract.

Her journey began at Nasikawa Vision Secondary School, where she first represented her school in rugby league.

After the 2021 Secondary School League season, she joined Vusu Raiders Rugby League Club, continuing to develop her game and pursue her ambition of playing at a higher level.

But away from rugby league, Vusama was dealing with challenges that tested her strength from a young age.

“I’ve faced difficulties in my life. I lost my dad at the age of four and was raised by my mom, a single parent since,” she said.

Raised by her mother, Vusama remained focused on her dreams.

Her determination eventually took her to the international stage when she was selected for the Fiji Bulikula women’s team for the 2023 South Pacific Games in the Solomon Islands.

The opportunity came with a sacrifice as Vusama did not sit her Year 13 examination that year after travelling with the national side, choosing to pursue the chance to represent Fiji.

That experience became an important turning point in her rugby league journey, opening the door to further opportunities beyond Fiji.

But Vusama’s journey was soon tested by a serious health setback.

She was admitted to intensive care after becoming ill and was later told she could no longer travel by plane.

For a player whose rugby league pathway was beginning to take her beyond Fiji, the setback could have brought her ambitions to a halt.

Her family remained a constant source of strength, supporting her through difficult periods and helping her travel to training each day, including providing bus fare so she could continue pursuing rugby league.

“I’m thankful for the support from my family for their upbringing and during the hard times,” she said.

Vusama continued to build her rugby league experience, with another opportunity coming in 2024 when she attended the Australia Rise Rookie squad.

In 2025, she travelled to Canada to play for the Bulikula, adding another international chapter to her development.

Those experiences have helped shape Vusama as a player and given her valuable exposure to rugby league outside Fiji.

Now she is back in Australia, but this time with an even bigger objective.

As one of five Bulikula players selected for the Rise Rookie Tour, Vusama wants to make the opportunity count.

“I don’t want to come back empty-handed. I want to achieve my goals and secure a contract with the NRLW,” she said.

For Vusama, the Australian tour is not simply another international experience.

It is a chance to showcase her ability, test herself against new competition and move closer to the professional career she has worked towards.

Her journey has taken her from school rugby league at Nasikawa Vision Secondary School, to Vusu Raiders, the Bulikula and international opportunities in the Solomon Islands, Australia and Canada.

Now, she wants the next chapter to be even bigger.

“To the young people out there, pursue your dreams,” Vusama said.

For the young woman from Naboutini, the message comes from experience.

She has faced loss, health challenges and personal difficulties, but each setback has strengthened her determination to keep moving forward.

Now, in Australia, Vusama has another opportunity to turn that resilience into achievement and take another step towards the dream she refuses to let go — earning an NRLW contract.

item.title: Cuvu storms into top 8
item.description: CUVU College head coach Luke Salaba has praised his side’s disciplined performance after they thrashed St John’s College Cawaci 55-7 to secure a place in next week’s Vodafone Deans under-18 quarter-finals at Lawaqa Park on Saturday. Salaba said his players executed their game plan well but stressed there was still room for improvement ahead of the knockout stages.
item.content:encoded:
CUVU College head coach Luke Salaba has praised his side’s disciplined performance after they thrashed St John’s College Cawaci 55-7 to secure a place in next week’s Vodafone Deans under-18 quarter-finals at Lawaqa Park on Saturday.

Salaba said his players executed their game plan well but stressed there was still room for improvement ahead of the knockout stages.

“It was a good effort from our boys. We did not underestimate Cawaci. Right now our focus is the quarter-final and we will work on our weaknesses.

“We will try to improve as we take one game at a time,” he said.

Cuvu dominated from the opening whistle, crossing for five first-half tries to take a commanding 33-7 lead at the break.

Josateki Toutou opened the scoring before Viliame Ratu added the conversion.

Waisake Tabua extended the lead with Cuvu’s second try, again converted by Ratu.

Waisale Nacola crossed for the third try with Ratu maintaining his perfect kicking record before Kamenieli Naikaniwasawasa powered over for the fourth, with Ratu adding another conversion.

Marika Senibua scored the fifth try before Ratu missed his first conversion attempt.

St John’s College Cawaci responded through Vilikesa Tokalauvere, with Suluo converting to leave the halftime score at 33-7.

Cuvu continued to dominate after the break as Naikaniwasawasa grabbed his second try of the match before Inoke Bolakania crossed for another five-pointer.

Jone Naivakarau added Cuvu’s eighth try, with the conversion successful, before Ro Viliame Mataitini completed the scoring with the ninth try as Cuvu sealed an emphatic 55-7 victory.

Despite the heavy defeat, Cawaci head coach Josaia Diani was pleased with his team’s effort.

“I’m impressed and satisfied with our players’ performance.

“This is one of our best games we have ever played.”

item.title: Delta Tigers maul City boys
item.description: STRATUM Construction Rewa FC delivered a dominant display to defeat Global Care Suva FC 4-0 in their Extra Premier League Round 16 encounter at Churchill Park yesterday. The Delta Tigers took control early and went into the halftime break with a 1-0 advantage after Josaia Sela found the back of the net.
item.content:encoded:
STRATUM Construction Rewa FC delivered a dominant display to defeat Global Care Suva FC 4-0 in their Extra Premier League Round 16 encounter at Churchill Park yesterday.

The Delta Tigers took control early and went into the halftime break with a 1-0 advantage after Josaia Sela found the back of the net.

Rewa returned with greater intensity in the second spell, extending their lead through Asivorosi Rabo before Semi Matalau added a third to put the contest beyond Suva’s reach.

Substitute Neemish Prasad completed the convincing victory with the fourth goal, capping off an impressive all-round team performance.

The result earned Rewa all three competition points and provided a timely confidence boost ahead of their OFC Men’s Champions League campaign, which begins at Churchill Park next weekend.

Rewa controlled possession for much of the match, creating several scoring opportunities while limiting Suva’s attacking threats to record a deserved clean sheet in front of their home supporters.

item.title: Mooar eyes Fijian coach
item.description: NEW Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar hopes to leave a legacy by helping develop a local coach capable of leading the club when his tenure comes to an end. Rather than focusing on personal achievements, Mooar said his greatest success would be seeing a Fijian take over the head coaching role in the future.
item.content:encoded:
NEW Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar hopes to leave a legacy by helping develop a local coach capable of leading the club when his tenure comes to an end.

Rather than focusing on personal achievements, Mooar said his greatest success would be seeing a Fijian take over the head coaching role in the future.

“I would love to see the next head coach of the Drua to be Fijian, and that would be a huge success for me,” Mooar said.

The former All Blacks assistant coach is determined to build a team culture centred on connection, pride and accountability, while strengthening the bond between the players and the wider Fijian community.

Mooar said he wanted the Drua to be recognised as a caring and united group that proudly represented not only the club but also the people of Fiji.

“We are an extension of our community, of our people. We are connected with our families, with the schools, with the villages and with the people of Fiji,” he said.

He added that his players would be encouraged to remain curious, work hard to improve every day and hold each other accountable to the team’s standards.

On the field, Mooar said the Drua would continue to embrace the exciting Fijian style of rugby while placing equal importance on the less glamorous aspects of the game.

“We will embrace the DNA of the Drua and the DNA of Fijian rugby, but we will also have the rock-hard work ethic to enjoy the grinding parts of the game.

“The set-piece, the defence and the work that no one sees getting done we will celebrate those moments.”

Looking ahead to the end of the 2027 season, Mooar hopes supporters will remember the Drua as a team that was exciting to watch and deeply connected to its fans.

“I hope people will say it has been awesome to come to Drua games and that they have loved every moment of watching the Drua play,” he added.

item.title: Ba on track to claim EPL title
item.description: BA is on track to end a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title after securing a crucial 2-1 victory over Labasa at Subrail Park yesterday. The Men in Black strengthened their position at the top of the points table with the win, putting themselves in a strong position with two matches remaining in the competition.
item.content:encoded:
BA is on track to end a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title after securing a crucial 2-1 victory over Labasa at Subrail Park yesterday.

The Men in Black strengthened their position at the top of the points table with the win, putting themselves in a strong position with two matches remaining in the competition.

Ba last won the league title in 2019 and is now within touching distance of reclaiming the crown.

The victory was particularly important as Ba and Labasa were battling for the top spot, with the Men in Black showing composure to claim all three points in Labasa.

The teams went into halftime locked at 1-1 before Ba found the decisive goal in the 76th minute.

Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar, however, was cautious about his side’s chances of winning the title.

“I will not say that at the moment. However, I will say that we want to be competitive during the season,” he said.

Mr Kumar said the team still had two matches to play and anything could happen.

“This was a turning point in the league, where Ba and Labasa were fighting for the top spot, and Ba came out victorious with a gallant performance today in Labasa.”

Ba’s latest victory follows its win over Labasa in the Fiji FACT semi-final last month.

Meanwhile, in another match played yesterday, Nadi edged Nasinu 3-2.
